title: Leaves Along the Path
cardDescription: Follow an autumn path through familiar tree names, leaf parts, colors, and the sounds of fallen leaves.
description: Follow an autumn path through familiar tree names, leaf parts, colors, and the sounds of fallen leaves.
focus: This puzzle looks at trees and leaves during a fall walk. Some answers name a tree or plant part; others describe a color or a route through the woods. Appearance varies with species and place.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for a tree, a plant part, or a color. Familiar short color words can help cross the longer leaf and woodland terms.
words: Flat plant part that may change color and fall in autumn
Tree whose sap is used to make a familiar sweet syrup
Tree often recognized by pale peeling bark
Shade tree traditionally associated with a spreading vase-shaped crown
Tree whose name also means powder left after a fire
Color of a stop signal and some autumn leaves
Rich yellow shade seen in some fall foliage
Yellow-orange color also named for fossilized tree resin
Reddish-brown shade associated with autumn leaves
Reddish-brown color named for oxidized iron
Branching line carrying materials through a leaf
Slender support connecting a leaf to the plant
Woody part extending from a tree's trunk
Overhead layer formed by the crowns of trees
Soft dry sound made by leaves moving together
Crackling sound made when stepping on dry leaves
Route followed by walkers through autumn woods
Garden tool with teeth used to gather fallen leaves
Heap of leaves gathered in one place

answerNotes.MAPLE: Maple names the tree associated with maple syrup. The clue uses a familiar product rather than one leaf color, which can vary.
answerNotes.ASH: Ash is a tree name and a word for residue after burning. The clue uses that shared spelling as a second route to the answer.
answerNotes.AMBER: Amber names both a yellow-orange color and fossilized resin. The color meaning fits this autumn setting.
answerNotes.CANOPY: A woodland canopy is formed by treetops overhead. It differs from the ground-level path beneath them.
answerNotes.RUSTLE: Rustle is a light dry movement sound. Crunch suggests sharper cracking under a foot, so the described action helps distinguish them.
answerNotes.RAKE: Rake names the toothed gathering tool here. It can also be a verb meaning to use that tool.

title: At the Autumn Farm Stand
cardDescription: Visit a fall farm stand through familiar crops, containers, and words for gathering and pressing fruit.
description: Visit a fall farm stand through familiar crops, containers, and words for gathering and pressing fruit.
focus: The clues follow a harvest from plants to containers and familiar products. Some words identify a crop or plant part, while others identify an action or a quantity used in selling produce.
solvingTip: Look for the difference between a whole crop, one part, a container, and an action. Short corn and fruit words can help cross the longer harvest terms.
words: Apple drink commonly sold at an American autumn farm stand
Tree fruit pressed for a familiar fall drink
Orchard fruit often narrower at the stem end than at the base
Large squash commonly associated with an orange autumn harvest
Garden crop that includes pumpkins and acorn varieties
Harvest crop with kernels growing in rows on a cob
Hard-shelled fruit often used for autumn decoration
Area planted with fruit trees for a harvest
U.S. dry-volume measure often associated with baskets of apples
Handled container used to gather ripe produce
Sturdy open container used to transport harvested fruit
Tall supporting stem left in a cornfield
Leafy outer covering removed from an ear of corn
One seed-like grain attached to a corn cob
Central support remaining after corn kernels are removed
Device used to squeeze liquid from apples
To gather fruit by removing it from a plant
Mature and ready for harvest, as fruit
Plants grown for food, considered collectively

answerNotes.CIDER: In American farm-stand use, cider commonly means an apple drink that may be unfiltered. Hard cider specifically indicates an alcoholic version.
answerNotes.BUSHEL: A bushel measures dry volume rather than a fixed weight. The weight of a bushel depends on the produce being measured.
answerNotes.HUSK: The husk is the leafy covering of an ear of corn. The cob is the central support inside the kernels.
answerNotes.KERNEL: A kernel is one individual grain on the cob. The clue asks for a single piece rather than the whole ear.
answerNotes.PRESS: Press names the squeezing device in this clue. It is a noun rather than an instruction to push something.
answerNotes.GOURD: Gourd is a broad name associated with hard-shelled fruits. The decorative context points to the item rather than a particular color or shape.

title: Woodland Neighbors in Fall
cardDescription: Meet familiar woodland animals through their shelters and the foods they find along a fall trail.
description: Meet familiar woodland animals through their shelters and the foods they find along a fall trail.
focus: The clues pair animal names with words for shelters and gathered food. Descriptions identify familiar features without assuming every animal follows the same seasonal routine.
solvingTip: Ask whether the clue names an animal, its home, or something gathered as food. Short food and shelter words can provide crossings for longer animal names.
words: Bushy-tailed rodent often seen gathering nuts in fall
Small striped rodent with cheek pouches
Woodland mammal with a masked face and ringed tail

Bird of prey often associated with rounded eyes and quiet flight

Small juicy fruit eaten by many wild animals
Plant structure that can be gathered as food by wildlife
Hair covering the body of many woodland mammals
Mark left in soft ground by an animal's foot

answerNotes.CHIPMUNK: Chipmunks are small striped rodents with cheek pouches. Those visible features distinguish the clue from the broader word squirrel.
answerNotes.RACCOON: A raccoon's facial mask and ringed tail are familiar markings. The clue uses both rather than relying on size alone.
answerNotes.CACHE: Cache is a hidden store, such as food kept for later. It sounds like cash but has a different spelling and meaning.
answerNotes.ACORN: An acorn is the nut of an oak. The tree named in the clue identifies the particular woodland food.
answerNotes.DEN: Den names an animal shelter here. It can also name a room in a house in another setting.
answerNotes.TRACK: Track names a footprint or other mark here. It is evidence left behind rather than the animal itself.

title: Ready for a Crisp Day
cardDescription: Get ready for a cool outing with familiar clothing, fabric, and fastening words.
description: Get ready for a cool outing with familiar clothing, fabric, and fastening words.
focus: This puzzle looks at garments and their parts. Some answers name something worn, while others name an edge, a closure, or a way garments are worn. The location and purpose in each clue help distinguish related items.
solvingTip: Check whether a clue asks for a whole garment, one part, or a way it is worn. Wrist, neck, and pocket locations can guide the short answers.
words: Knitted upper-body garment worn on a cool day
Sweater that opens down the front
Long piece of fabric wrapped around the neck
Hand covering with a separate thumb and one shared finger space
Hand covering with a separate section for each finger
Outer garment worn over other clothes
Short outer garment commonly ending near the hips
Cloth foot covering worn inside a shoe or boot
Sheep's fiber used in some warm clothing

Describing fabric formed from interlocking yarn loops

Part of a shirt or coat around the neck

Small sewn compartment for carrying something in a garment
Head covering attached to a coat or sweatshirt
One garment worn over or under another
To wind a scarf around the neck

answerNotes.CARDIGAN: A cardigan opens at the front. A pullover goes over the head instead, so the opening is the clue's defining feature.
answerNotes.MITTEN: A mitten gives the fingers one shared space. A glove has individual finger sections, which distinguishes the two coverings.
answerNotes.FLEECE: Fleece names a soft fabric in this clue. The same word can also refer to a sheep's woolly coat.
answerNotes.CUFF: A cuff is located at a sleeve's end. Collar identifies the neck area, so the body location matters.
answerNotes.LAYER: Layer names one garment in a combination here. The clue describes a relative position rather than a particular fabric.
answerNotes.HOOD: A hood is attached to a garment in this clue. It differs from a separate hat put on independently.

title: An Autumn Front Porch
cardDescription: Picture an autumn porch with familiar flowers, pumpkins, decorations, and the parts of an entrance.
description: Picture an autumn porch with familiar flowers, pumpkins, decorations, and the parts of an entrance.
focus: The clues bring together a doorway setting and familiar seasonal objects. Some answers name a display item, while others name a part of the porch or a simple action.
solvingTip: Look for a place, an object, a plant part, or an action. A ring-shaped decoration and a potted fall flower have different names. Short entrance words can help cross longer decorations.
words: Light with a protective housing that can be carried or hung
Round squash often hollowed into a fall lantern
Hard-shelled fruit placed in many autumn displays
Ring-shaped decoration hung on a front door
Greeting commonly printed on a doorstep mat
Movable panel opened to enter a home
Covered entrance area outside a house
One raised level climbed toward a doorway
Long support along the side of porch steps
Small floor covering laid outside an entrance
Container holding a flowering plant on a porch
Short name for a chrysanthemum grown for fall flowers
Dried forage sometimes displayed in compact bales
Tightly packed bundle of hay or straw
Decorative fabric strip wrapped around a seasonal display
Looped ribbon knot used as a decoration
To cut a design into a pumpkin's surface
Eyes, nose, and mouth arranged as a pumpkin design
Plant support left attached at the top of a pumpkin
One small plant structure inside a pumpkin

answerNotes.MUM: Mum is a familiar shortened name for chrysanthemum. In this flower clue it does not mean a parent or keeping quiet.
answerNotes.WREATH: A wreath has a ring form. A bow is a looped knot, so the shape helps distinguish two doorway decorations.
answerNotes.BALE: A bale is a compact bound bundle. It names the packaged form rather than the material inside it.
answerNotes.BOW: Bow means a looped ribbon knot and rhymes with go here. The porch-display setting selects that meaning.
answerNotes.STEM: A pumpkin stem is the remaining plant support at its top. It is a plant part rather than a carved decoration.
answerNotes.CARVE: Carve describes cutting a design into a material. The clue identifies the action without giving a sequence of carving instructions.
